topic: Mars Climate Orbiter: the unit mix-up that lost a spacecraft (1999)
claim: NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter was lost on Sept. 23, 1999 because thruster data was delivered in pound-force seconds instead of the specified newton-seconds, so its path took it far lower over Mars than planned.

beats.caption: ONE WRONG UNIT
beats.vo: One wrong unit lost a spaceship.

beats.caption: DECEMBER 11, 1998
beats.vo: NASA launched Mars Climate Orbiter on December eleventh, nineteen ninety-eight. Nine months to Mars.

beats.caption: POUNDS VS NEWTONS
beats.vo: Ground software gave thruster data in pound-seconds. The navigation software expected newton-seconds. One pound-force is four point four five newtons.

beats.caption: TOO LOW
beats.vo: The plan was two hundred twenty-six kilometers above Mars. The real path dipped to fifty-seven. The lowest survivable was eighty.

beats.caption: SEPTEMBER 23, 1999
beats.vo: On September twenty-third, nineteen ninety-nine, the signal vanished, forty-nine seconds early.

beats.caption: CHECK YOUR UNITS
beats.vo: A spaceship, lost to a unit mix-up. Always check your units.

sources.text: NASA Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board, Phase I Report, Nov. 10, 1999 (launch Dec. 11, 1998; carrier signal last seen 09:04:52 UTC Sept. 23, 1999, 49 s earlier than predicted; Small Forces file in lb-sec instead of N-sec, factor 4.45; planned first periapsis 226 km, minimum survivable 80 km, after-the-fact estimate 57 km): https://llis.nasa.gov/llis_lib/pdf/1009464main1_0641-mr.pdf
NASA Science, Mars Climate Orbiter (English vs metric units error; spacecraft burned up in Mars' atmosphere): https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-climate-orbiter/
